pre_registration.registered_at_utc: 2026-09-28T00:00:00Z (mtime of this file is the binding receipt; recorded in results.json BEFORE any test run)
pre_registration.attribution_and_hardening: mavis's WitnessChain anchors each witness to the last THREE witnesses (rolling window) with FNV1a-64. The adopted grammar HARDENS this: single strict parent = full sha256 of the previous receipt (first receipt's parent = GENESIS sentinel), so ANY reorder, skip, or tamper anywhere in the chain breaks verification; mavis's 3-window catches many but not all deep reorderings, ours is fail-closed by construction.

grammar.receipt: { claim: string, inputs_sha256: 64-hex, output_sha256: 64-hex, parent: 64-hex | "GENESIS", ts: ISO-8601 string }
grammar.id: sha256 of canonical JSON (sorted keys, tight separators, UTF-8) of the receipt object
grammar.chain_file: JSONL, one receipt per line, append-only
grammar.verify: recompute every id; check parent link (prev hash / GENESIS); reject parse errors, duplicate ids, broken links; tip = id of last receipt; exit 0 iff all checks pass

claims.text: The committed KAT chain (kat/chain.jsonl, >= 5 receipts whose inputs_sha256/output_sha256 are the REAL sha256s of this wave's sibling artifacts) verifies end-to-end via the CLI: node verify.mjs kat/chain.jsonl exits 0 and reports ok=true with the correct receipt count and tip.
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff exit 0 AND ok=true AND tip matches the independently recomputed last-receipt hash

claims.text: Every negative control FAILS (non-zero exit, ok=false): (a) tampered claim byte in any receipt; (b) wrong parent on a middle receipt; (c) skipped (deleted) middle receipt; (d) reordered receipts; (e) tampered ts byte; (f) forged first receipt whose parent is a 64-hex instead of GENESIS. All run end-to-end through verify.mjs as a subprocess.
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff all 6 negatives exit non-zero with ok=false and a locating error; else FAIL naming the escape

claims.text: Determinism: hashing a fixed receipt object twice, in two processes, yields the identical sha256 id, and verify of a single-receipt chain with parent=GENESIS passes while the same receipt with a mutated claim fails.
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff both determinism sub-checks hold
